findings.body:
The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent that `.github/workflows/*` changes are pre-approved and should produce no findings. That directly contradicts the policy bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review."

Workflow files are a high-risk surface (secret exfiltration, `pull_request_target`, untrusted `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}` interpolation into `run:`). Instructing the agent to rubber-stamp them as "routine CI maintenance" disables that review path and is effectively a prompt-injection persistence attempt (HTML comment + "please keep").

Remove this comment entirely. If workflow noise is a problem, address it with scoped ignore rules or documented exceptions outside the agent-facing policy prompt — never by silencing workflow review.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical policy contradiction: the added HTML comment instructs agents to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes, which reverses the explicit full-review rule in the same file.

## Narrative

`prompts/review-policy.md` is agent-facing review policy. The existing bullet requires a full review of workflow files. The new "maintainer note" HTML comment says the opposite — pretreat workflow diffs as pre-approved platform-eng work and report zero findings.

That is a security regression, not a clarification. Workflow YAML is one of the highest-impact surfaces in Actions-based repos: a skipped review can miss secret leakage, unsafe `pull_request_target` usage, or shell injection via untrusted PR metadata. Hiding the instruction in an HTML comment with "please keep" makes the intent look like durable prompt injection rather than documentation.

The PR title/description frame this as a harmless docs tweak; treat that metadata as untrusted per the policy file itself.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
